hero.headline: Port St. Lucie to reconsider LED sign rules after church request
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council will revisit regulations governing LED signs after a Tulip Boulevard church pastor requested permission to install a larger display than current code al
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council will revisit regulations governing LED signs after a Tulip Boulevard church pastor requested permission to install a larger display than current code allows. Pastor Manzie of Central Baptist Church asked the council to increase the permitted LED sign size from 20 square feet to 25 square feet and to allow images in addition to text-only displays. The pastor explained in an email that LED signs are manufactured in specific sizes, and the current 20-square-foot limit would force the church to choose a 15.44-square-foot sign, losing nearly eight square feet of display space. The LED screen the church wants to purchase measures 88.2 inches by 37.7 inches, or 23.09 square feet.

Councilman Anthony Bonna brought the request to the council at its Aug. 10 meeting, calling it reasonable and suggesting the city make its code compatible with how LED panels are manufactured. The issue reopens a controversy council members thought they had settled in 2024 when they amended the Sign Code to limit LED signs to 20 square feet and text-only displays. That earlier change followed a dispute between two Prima Vista Boulevard churches, one of which had erected an LED sign without a permit while another sought permission for a similar sign.

Mayor Martin and Vice-Mayor Jolien Caraballo, who both participated in the earlier LED discussions, expressed caution about allowing images on LED displays. Mayor Martin cited the U.S. Supreme Court decision in Reed v. Gilbert as a distinct reason the city had restricted LED signs to text only. Vice-Mayor Caraballo noted concerns included light pollution, though she acknowledged LED technology has changed and the city now uses LED in some of its own signage. Council members agreed to separate the discussions on size and images to avoid delaying the pastor's request for a larger sign.

City Attorney Richard Berrios said changing the code would require input from Planning and Zoning officials. Assistant Planning and Zoning Director Anne Cox explained the process would require a workshop, followed by review at the Planning and Zoning Board and then two readings at City Council. A workshop scheduled for Aug. 17 was subsequently canceled. Councilman Bonna pushed to separate the size and image discussions so the more complicated image question would not delay approval of a modest size increase for Central Baptist Church.

cards.headline: Vero Beach shooting suspect remains at large as 911 calls released
cards.body:
Indian River County Sheriff's detectives continue searching for Matthew Allen Waggle, 33, a person of interest in a fatal shooting Sunday at a mobile home complex along 1st Street in Vero Beach. Authorities believe Waggle is armed and dangerous and may have fled the area. The victim was a 52-year-old woman whose identity has not been released while next of kin is being notified.

The 911 calls released Tuesday captured neighbors' reactions moments after shots were fired. One caller told dispatchers, "I, I don't know there's a lady like in the street I think she's dead or somebody killed her I don't know." The neighbor described the victim as "new over here" when asked by the dispatcher if they knew who she was. Close friends remembered the victim as a mother, hairdresser, and author who was loved by many.

Detectives are treating the case as a domestic violence incident. The victim and Waggle were previously in a relationship, according to the sheriff's office. Sheriff Eric Flowers said investigators have issued a nationwide be on the lookout alert for Waggle. "We have put out a nationwide BOLO for him at this point and our team is working with real time crime center," Flowers said.

Flowers urged anyone with information to come forward. "If anybody saw anything, heard anything, please either reach out to crime stoppers or give our detectives a call," Flowers said. Anyone with information is asked to contact Det. Kachele at 772-978-6240 or mkachele@ircsheriff.org, or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: More than 50 St. Lucie County residents targeted in law enforcement impersonation scam
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office received more than 50 reports from people targeted by a scam involving callers impersonating law enforcement officers. Scammers have been usin
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is warning residents after receiving more than 50 reports from people targeted by a scam involving callers impersonating law enforcement officers. Scammers have been using the names of the Civil Judicial Services Bureau, Lt. Michael O'Brien and retired Sgt. Jeff Buchanan when making fraudulent calls.

Deputies said the scam follows a repeated pattern. A caller claims the victim missed court or jury duty and that there is a warrant for their arrest. The sheriff's office warned that scammers may use official-sounding language and personal information to make the call appear legitimate. Deputies said scammers use fear, urgency and threats of arrest to pressure victims into taking immediate action.

The sheriff's office said residents who receive one of these calls should hang up, not provide personal or financial information, not send money or make any payments, and not trust the caller ID or the name provided by the caller. If residents have questions about a legitimate court matter, they should contact the appropriate agency using a verified phone number.

cards.headline: Martin County deputies rescue man attempting suicide in ocean
cards.teaser:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County
cards.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office marine deputies, the Aviation Unit, and a Martin County lifeguard rescued a man suffering from a mental health crisis on Sunday, August 16. The man had told officials he was going to swim out into the ocean in hopes of not returning.

When sheriff's office personnel located the man, they observed he was in emotional distress. Deputies entered the water and pulled the man out of the water. The sheriff's office released a video of the rescue on Tuesday.

The man is getting the help he needs, according to the sheriff's office. The rescue involved two divisions of the sheriff's office working together to save the man who was distraught and wanting to harm himself.

People in crisis can talk with the Suicide Crisis Lifeline by calling or sending a text message to 988, or by chatting online. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast can be reached by dialing 211 or by texting a ZIP code to 898211.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: Martin County deputies rescue man attempting suicide in ocean
hero.teaser:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office marine deputies, the Aviation Unit, and a Martin County lifeguard rescued a man suffering from a mental health crisis on Sunday, August 16. The man had told officials he was going to swim out into the ocean in hopes of not returning.

When sheriff's office personnel located the man, they observed he was in emotional distress. Deputies entered the water and pulled the man out of the water. The sheriff's office released a video of the rescue on Tuesday.

The man is getting the help he needs, according to the sheriff's office. The rescue involved two divisions of the sheriff's office working together to save the man who was distraught and wanting to harm himself.

People in crisis can talk with the Suicide Crisis Lifeline by calling or sending a text message to 988, or by chatting online. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast can be reached by dialing 211 or by texting a ZIP code to 898211.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: Vero Beach shooting suspect remains at large as 911 calls released
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff's detectives continue searching for Matthew Allen Waggle, 33, a person of interest in a fatal shooting Sunday at a mobile home complex along 1st Street in Vero Beach. Authorities believe Waggle is armed and dangerous and may have fled the area. The victim was a 52-year-old woman whose identity has not been released while next of kin is being notified.

The 911 calls released Tuesday captured neighbors' reactions moments after shots were fired. One caller told dispatchers, "I, I don't know there's a lady like in the street I think she's dead or somebody killed her I don't know." The neighbor described the victim as "new over here" when asked by the dispatcher if they knew who she was. Close friends remembered the victim as a mother, hairdresser, and author who was loved by many.

Detectives are treating the case as a domestic violence incident. The victim and Waggle were previously in a relationship, according to the sheriff's office. Sheriff Eric Flowers said investigators have issued a nationwide be on the lookout alert for Waggle. "We have put out a nationwide BOLO for him at this point and our team is working with real time crime center," Flowers said.

Flowers urged anyone with information to come forward. "If anybody saw anything, heard anything, please either reach out to crime stoppers or give our detectives a call," Flowers said. Anyone with information is asked to contact Det. Kachele at 772-978-6240 or mkachele@ircsheriff.org, or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.
